page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The smoker
title: The smoker
description:
Anna is off to meet Mr Ingle, the warehouse manager, to discuss stock management. But she finds him doing something dangerous and illegal! She needs to ask him to stop it politely. Find out how she makes this request.
This episode focuses on politely asking a member of your team not to do something.
phrases: Would you mind not doing that please?
I'm afraid it's against company policy.
Sorry to have to ask you this but…

listening_challenge.question:
What other word does Anna use to mean 'put out your cigarette'?
To extinguish.
listening_challenge.answer:
What other word does Anna use to mean 'put out your cigarette'?
To extinguish.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello, welcome back to Tip Top Trading where Anna is going downstairs to speak to warehouse manager, Mr Ingle. You’re looking a bit nervous…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I am. Denise says if I speak to him in the wrong way, he might bite my head off!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Relax Anna. It’s just an expression to mean he might be a bit aggressive.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You’ll be fine, just use the right polite phrases… oh, and smile!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, I will. Oh look here I am…
(Warehouse door opens)

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mr Ingle, are you there? I’d be most grateful if you could give me some… oh, what’s that smell… and smoke… Mr Ingle!

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Oh, oh (coughs)

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mr Ingle. You’re smoking!

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Well… it’s my lunch break… so I’m allowed to smoke a cigarette, aren’t I?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Really? Are you sure?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: No, he’s not Anna! Smoking inside a public building is illegal – it’s against the law. It’s dangerous too - you’ve got to do something about this.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. Mmm, er, Mr Ingle, you mustn’t smoke… it’s wrong.

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Says who?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, Me?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna. You’ll have to do better than that. Be polite, but be firm too. Try saying, ‘would you mind not doing that please?’

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I’ll try. Mr Ingle, would you mind not doing that please?

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Why’s that then?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: He’s not being very nice is he? You need to give your reasons. Say, ‘I’m afraid it’s against company policy’. Go on you can do it.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mr Ingle… I’m afraid it’s against company policy. And… it is actually against the law to smoke here… and… it’s not a nice smell, is it?

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Well, smells OK to me.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I’m sorry to have to ask you this but you need to put it out.

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Put what out – the cat?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No. You need to extinguish your cigarette… please.

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Says who?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I’m sure your team wouldn’t like to see you breaking the law and besides, it could cause a fire. That would be awful.

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Yeah, I suppose it would.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I could get you some nicotine gum if you like?

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: No, it’s OK. I’ll stub it out… as you asked so nicely.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you Mr Ingle. We’ll keep it a secret this time, but please don’t do it again. I’m afraid it’s just not permitted on company premises.

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Yeah, whatever!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh and Mr Ingle, I still really like your overalls. Bye!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Nice one Anna. You dealt with Mr Ingle really well. You kept your cool and explained the reasons why he shouldn’t smoke. Let’s hope he doesn’t do it again Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I hope not. I hate the smell of cigarette smoke. But I never got to ask him about stock management.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, maybe it’s best to leave it for another time?

transcript.speaker: Anna’s had a tricky day so far dealing with Mr Ingle but she was firm and fair in the language she used. Here’s a reminder of the phrases she used
transcript.text:
Would you mind not doing that please?
I’m afraid it’s against company policy.
I’m afraid it’s not permitted.
Sorry to have to ask you this but…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah Anna, there you are…. (sniffing) Have you been smoking?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You smell of cigarette smoke. Look, I know you’re under pressure – but smoking in the building is not permitted.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Bbbut…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: We take this very seriously. You had better step in to my office and we’ll talk about this.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear! Anna’s in trouble for no reason. Let’s hope she explains the mix-up, but that means telling Paul about Mr Ingle smoking. This is going to be difficult. Until next time, bye!
